nodes.label: Direct-First Proxy Escalation Strategy
nodes.rationale: Attempt 1 is always direct; only after waiting out the ladder delay does the next attempt use a proxy, so the proxy switch reads as normal retry behavior rather than an evasion burst.

nodes.label: Celery ETA/Countdown Is Unsafe For Backoff
nodes.rationale: With the Redis broker, ETA-scheduled tasks are held in worker memory until due; a restart during a long wait silently drops or duplicates it. Postgres tracks.scheduled_at must be the sole source of truth so the schedule survives any restart.
nodes.norm_label: celery eta/countdown is unsafe for backoff

nodes.label: Server-to-Server Login Pattern
nodes.rationale: Upstream Set-Cookie: VB-AUTH=...; Domain=localhost can never be stored by a browser on a different domain, so login must happen server-to-server and spotdl-web mints its own session cookie rather than forwarding VB-AUTH to the browser.

nodes.label: Email Allowlist Authorization Gate
nodes.rationale: POST /auth/register is public on vb2007.hu-api, so a successful upstream login only proves the account is real, not that the person may use spotdl-web; ALLOWED_EMAILS is the actual authorization gate, and rejection must be indistinguishable from a wrong password.

nodes.label: worker-dl Single-Concurrency Rationale
nodes.rationale: worker-dl deliberately runs --concurrency=1 --prefetch-multiplier=1 because concurrency itself is rate-limit exposure; serialized downloads are safer than throughput.

nodes.label: Manual Breaker Release ≠ Earned Recovery
nodes.rationale: Manual breaker release clears the countdown early but does not reset consecutive_failures or breaker_trip_count, since a manual release is not an earned recovery — the next failure re-trips at the next escalation step, not back at 30m.
